<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05f7758f054d70f3ba0f709b37423124be3e6e3d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `55f6fc2730781c03717264b72f9acfe8e81ec62f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-node.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-written-address-channels.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-email-field-recipient.integration.test.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts, examples/app-showcase/test/approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/services/service-messaging/src/recipient-resolver.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/inbox-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/email-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/sms-channel.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/value-slot-map.ts, scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs, examples/app-showcase/test/inert-wirings.test.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/security/demo-personas.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/data/seed/index.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/security/seed-approval-demo.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/ensure-default-organization.ts, .changeset/25758-notify-written-address-no-email-channel.md (prose face, read for ②)

Inputs: card #25758 body and comments 6396218293, 6408881630, 6410135308; PR #25964 body, file list and `git diff origin/main...55f6fc27`; the 54 check-runs on the head (all concluded: 0 failed, 0 in progress; `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and its 8 shards, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` all `success`). The head is option B: commits `d352c68a` (computed recipients judged too) and `55f6fc27` (the showcase test seeds a user). The A subset is the head minus those two.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set and run-time changes the diff implies (read in `notify-node.ts` at the head against the messaging code on `main`):**

| notify node | recipient | before (main) | after (head) | judgment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` absent, `['inbox']`, or `sms` | bare address, no `sys_user.email` matches | resolver keeps it verbatim (`recipient-resolver.ts` `resolveEmail`), inbox writes a row with `user_id` = the address (`inbox-channel.ts:149`, `:205`); sms fails the delivery row (`no phone number for recipient`); node reports success | node fails before `emit`; message names the node, the channels or their absence, each such recipient in backticks, `(no user holds that address)`, and the fix (add `email`, or a user id / `role:NAME` / the held address bare); nothing written, nothing mailed (test A, 5 cases + the list case) | right. Only the email channel sends to an address (`email-channel.ts` `EMAIL_SHAPE(recipient)` branch); inbox and sms deliver to a user id. The lookup is the resolver's own (`sys_user` by `email`, `fields: ['id']`, system read). |
| same | bare address a user holds | resolver maps it to the user id; that user's inbox | unchanged (test B) | right |
| same | `user:ADDRESS`, held or not | resolver strips `user:` and hands the address on as an id with no lookup; junk row; success | node fails outright, `(user: takes a user id, not an email address)` (test A, 2 cases) | right in substance and consistent with `mailedAddressOf`, which already reads `user:a@b.c` as an address for the ruling-B screen and the email channel. One accept-set edge, noted not blocking: a `sys_user.id` that is itself address-shaped is refused without an id lookup; no in-repo producer writes `user:` plus an address (`git grep` on main finds only DSN examples). |
| same | no data engine, or the lookup throws | inbox not persisted (warn) or junk row; success | node fails, the message says the address could not be checked (test D; E5 of the email-field suite) | right: parity with `screenComputedAddresses`. Cosmetic: with no data engine the loop returns on the first bare address, so a `user:ADDRESS` entry collected before it is not named in that one message; the node still fails. |
| `channels` include `email` (alone or with `inbox`) | written-out address | sent as written (ruling B) | unchanged: `refuseUndeliverableAddresses` runs only under `!mails` (test C, 2 cases) | right |
| `channels` include `email` | computed address no user holds | fails through the ruling-B screen pointing to `{ emailField }` | unchanged (test E, last case) | right |
| `channels` absent, `['inbox']`, or `sms` | address a CEL envelope computes, no user holds it | goes to messaging as before; junk row; success (E5 on main pinned exactly this, per ruling A on #25647 as the dev read it) | **B only**: node fails, named by `recipients[i] evaluated to an email address — source: ...`, never the value (test E, 3 cases, `not.toContain('stranger@outside.example')`) | code is right and the value never leaks (`nameOf` reads `what` and `source` only; the only text not under the node's control is `err.message` on a thrown lookup, the same exposure the ruling-B screen already has). Whether this behaviour may land is ③ F1. |
| same | computed address a user holds | that user's inbox | unchanged (test E, held case) | right |

**Email-channel default and channel list.** `MessagingService.emit` defaults `channels` to `['inbox']` (`messaging-service.ts:1114`); `messaging-service-plugin.ts` registers `inbox` directly and `email`/`sms` through lazy providers; no fourth channel exists in the repo. The node reads `channels` raw (`toStringList`, static routing) and tests `includes('email')`, so the `mails` / `!mails` split is exhaustive and the where-clause text (`names no channels, so it delivers to the inbox, the default` versus `names channels ... and not email`) is accurate. Never re-routed: the node adds no channel (test A asserts `mailed` is empty on every refusal).

**Value-expression path.** `resolveRecipients` evaluates each envelope through `resolveValueSlot` (one evaluator, `value-slot-map.ts`), and only then reads the string with `mailedAddressOf`. The head moves the `mailedAddressOf` call out from under `isExpressionEnvelopeShaped(raw)` so a written string is read too; `computed` keeps its old population (envelope only), `addressed` takes both with provenance. `screenComputedAddresses` still consumes `computed` on a mailing node; nothing about the ruling-B screen moved. Right.

**Existing-test edits: fixes of off-contract fixtures, not loosening.**
- `notify-email-field-recipient.integration.test.ts` E5 (B only): on `main` it asserted `run.success === true` and `emitted[0].audience` equal to `['stranger@outside.example']` on an inbox node, i.e. it pinned the junk-row behaviour. The head asserts failure, no emit, and the undeliverable message rather than the mail-screen message (`bootUnchecked` has no data service, so the no-engine branch answers). Stronger, and it is the ruling-A pin flipped to B; on the A subset it stays as on `main`.
- `approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts` (B only): on `main` both assertions expected `notice.user_id` to be the literal `'grace@example.com'`, the unreadable row. The head seeds `usr_grace` holding that address through the driver before any run (data at rest) and asserts the user id. Stronger. But see F1: this makes the test's world consistent while the showcase's own seed is not.
- `flows/index.ts` `alert_exec`: `'exec@example.com'` on the inbox default becomes `'role:owner'`. `role:` expands through `sys_member` where `role = owner` in the run's tenant (`recipient-resolver.ts` `resolveRole`), and `ensure-default-organization.ts` inserts the admin's `sys_member { role: 'owner' }` row on the Default Organization. A producer fix, not a loosening. The three-line comment names the card number in source; AGENTS.md's no-tracker-number rule is for rules and runtime strings, and the codebase uses `[#NNNN]` code comments throughout, so no flag.

**Pinned-contract rows.** One row added to `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: `(notify-written-address-channels.integration.test.ts, findOne, pinned: 1)`, placed where the gate's sort (file, then verb; `check-engine-double-contract.mjs:2627`) puts it, between `notify-organization-stamp` and `notify-zero-delivery-visibility`. The test's double declares `insert`/`find`/`findOne` and its `findOne` calls `assertEngineFindOnePredicate(object, query)` imported from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, one of the slice's accepted modules, so PINNED and RETAINED both hold. `Lint & Repo Gates` is `success` on the head. Right.

**Would the A subset pass?** On the code read, yes: 47c6ea05 + e6878f86 + 011221d3 carry the written-out refusal, the new test's A to D cases, the ledger row, the `alert_exec` fix and a changeset whose text makes no claim about computed recipients. Its gate verdicts on its own head are not among this record's inputs (only the head's check-runs are), so an A record must be rendered on A's head once it exists. F6 below carries over to A as a disclosure item, not a blocker.

**Why the head as it stands fails (B).** The B changeset's "Who moves" paragraph states: the app-showcase's inbox nodes whose expressions read `record.owner` or `record.assignee` evaluate to addresses its seeds provision as users, pinned by `inert-wirings.test.ts`, so they keep delivering. Read in the cited code, that is false for one live producer:
- `inert-wirings.test.ts` §5 carries `KNOWN_EXEMPT = new Set(['showcase_invoice.owner'])`, and `demo-personas.ts` explains it is left addressed to non-users knowingly (the ADR-0055 isolation demo).
- `data/seed/index.ts` writes `showcase_invoice.owner` as `ada@example.com`, `linus@example.com`, `grace@example.com`; `PROVISIONED_USER_EMAILS` is `admin@objectos.ai`, `phone.demo@example.com`, `auditor.demo@example.com`.
- `InvoiceDualSignoffFlow` (`showcase_invoice_signoff`) node `notify_cleared` is `channels: ['inbox']` with `recipients: [{ cel: has(record.owner) ? record.owner : null }]`, and `seed-approval-demo.ts` opens a sign-off run on a seeded `sent` invoice at boot.
So under B, approving a seeded invoice fails the run at `notify_cleared` with `(no user holds that address)` unless an operator has signed up as that owner. Before, it wrote the junk row and succeeded. Failing loud is the rule this PR adopts, so the behaviour is not wrong in itself, but: the diff moves a live in-repo producer it neither names nor fixes (the `alert_exec` fix shows the PR knows the producer is its job: Prime Directives #10 and #12), the changeset publishes the opposite claim into `CHANGELOG.md`, and the option-B recommendation on the card rests on the same misreading of the §5 pin. No gate on the head exercises that approval (the dogfood isolation test pins owners and does not approve; the showcase test suite seeds its own Grace), so `Dogfood Regression Gate: success` says nothing about it, and the dev report says the dogfood battery was not re-run on the B commits locally.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/service-automation` `patch`, title with `!`, bold `BREAKING (run time)` line, `Clause-②: no (narrowing: ...)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial declarations, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` (a category `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` lists). AGENTS.md: a non-protocol change, breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and disposition; `none` takes `patch`. Level right. `Check Changeset` is `success` (two runs on the head).
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: the parse, `os validate` and every spec schema are unchanged; what moves is a run-time refusal of a value the contract still accepts. Precedent PR #25954 (`073f08b3`, on `main`) used exactly this pairing for a run-time refusal. Accepted, with the note that the `domain:spec` half (refusal at validate/publish) will be `narrowed` and at least `minor` when it lands.
- PR body `Clause-②: no (narrowing: ...)` line: present, line-initial, same shape as #25954; it names the computed arm too (B). The recogniser's `--paths` mode refused these paths and asked for the face to be read off the `Clause-②:` line, which carries `(narrowing)`: the narrowing face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, this record's tier.
- Title `!`: matches the BREAKING banner. Right.
- The changeset's substance under B carries the false "keep delivering" sentence (①). Under A (47c6ea05's text) the body is accurate: it names `alert_exec` and nothing else moves in the repo except F6.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F1 (report `open_questions`, `needs_decision`, A versus B): escalated to the maintainer, with a correction to the brief it was handed.** The recommendation says seeded owners are provisioned and pinned by `inert-wirings.test.ts`; that pin exempts `showcase_invoice.owner` by design, and B as implemented makes the seeded Invoice Dual Sign-off demo fail at `notify_cleared` (①). The maintainer's choice should weigh that fact. If B is chosen, the same PR must move `notify_cleared` (or state in the changeset that the demo now fails loud until the operator signs up as the owner) and rewrite the "Who moves" sentence; this record does not stand in for that word, and B must not be landed on it. Ruling A on #25647 (`6393736930`), as the dev read it in the comment 47c6ea05 wrote and `d352c68a` deleted, leaves computed recipients on a non-mailing node to messaging as before; B refines it. A maintainer refinement is the only thing that lifts that.
- **F2 (report DEPARTURE: `Clause-②: no` on the claim became `no (narrowing: ...)`):** right. A run that completed now fails at this node; the arm is owed and the review with it. Accepted.
- **F3 (report "reading chosen": written-out address read as an address no user holds):** matches the card's title and the triage's "a written-out address on a node with no email channel lands in an inbox nobody reads"; a held address still reaches its user (test B). Accepted.
- **F4 (`out_of_scope_findings` 1: `io-node-config.zod.ts` describe text):** the `domain:spec` half's carrier is named on the card by the claim (`No packages/spec/**`). Accepted as not this PR's.
- **F5 (`out_of_scope_findings` 2: inbox + email both named, unheld address mailed and a junk inbox row still written):** reproducible defect with no carrier (`承接者:无`, "noted, not filed"). Prime Directive #10 asks for an issue, not a note. Escalated: file a card.
- **F6 (not in the report): four more written-out inbox nodes in the showcase.** `ScheduledDigestFlow` `digest`, `ProjectEscalationFlow` `log_fail`, `ReleaseSignoffFlow` `notify_done`, `InquiryPurgeFlow` report node all write `'admin@objectos.ai'` on inbox-only nodes. `demo-personas.ts` registers `ADMIN_EMAIL` as provisioned on a dev boot (`maybeSeedDevAdmin`, gated on `NODE_ENV === 'development'`), so they hold where the showcase documents itself as running; on a non-dev boot they now fail loud instead of writing junk, which is the rule. Neither the PR body nor the changeset names them. Disclose in the changeset; applies to A and B alike.
- **F7 (report `dogfood_battery`): run at 47c6ea05 only; not re-run on `d352c68a`/`55f6fc27`.** The head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success`, but no gate approves a seeded invoice, so green there is not evidence on F1.
- **F8 (branch):** `claude/project-thread-hdpxcs` is the harness-pinned branch, not `claude/issue-25758-*`; the claim comment `6408881630` is the identity record and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` is `success`. Accepted.
- The PR is a draft and not governed-surface; nothing here is a seat act. No GitHub write, no local run, no checkout was made for this record.
